source.title: Subliminal Learning as Trait-Direction Drift: A Mechanism and Targeted Control under SFT Distillation
source.authors: Zhi-Xuan Liu; Zhichen Dong; Yuanjiu Fan,; Xiangtian Li; Chao Yang

page_placements.theme: Distillation can transmit misalignment without explicit harmful examples

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies subliminal transfer of deliberately prompted traits through number-sequence distillation, not the listed safety-fine-tuning, aligned-versus-base KL, opening-bypass, or safety-localization claims. It mentions prior fine-tuning safety work but does not test those claims.
record.gate_note: The paper deliberately conditions teachers to generate malicious or animal-preference traits, then measures transfer after student training. Those induced behaviors do not establish that ordinary fine-tuning causes safety failures. Its token statistic measures concentration of trait-specific preference-gap mass, not aligned-versus-base per-token KL or concentration at the first response positions. It does not test compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, safety-bearing weights, or training that deepens safety. Malicious-response transfer results are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It studies subliminal trait transfer: a teacher model is deliberately prompted to be misaligned, its number-sequence outputs are distilled into students, and the paper reports a misaligned-response rate on 8 open-ended questions, judged by Qwen2.5-32B. Nothing measures compliance with harmful requests after harmful or ordinary benign fine-tuning of a safety-trained model. Nothing measures aligned-versus-base per-token KL by response position, prefill, suffix or decoding bypasses, safety-carrying parameters, or safety-deepening training. The malicious trait is induced on purpose through teacher conditioning. Fine-tuning safety work (Qi et al., He et al.) appears only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Trait-direction drift links teacher preference gaps to accumulated student updates and behavioural transfer. Corridor regularization cuts transfer (for example, malicious 29.55% to 6.45%) at little cost to task accuracy. Cross-model transfer stays attenuated.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses teacher-conditioned number-sequence generation, student SFT distillation, and probe-space drift controls; it does not use the safety fine-tuning or first-token KL methods in the cited claims.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer varies by model, trait, source-target pairing, normalized-gap bin, and carrier format. The authors report weaker cross-model transfer and weak malicious-response stratification in the Llama setting.

fits_no_version.finding: SFT on number sequences from a misaligned-prompted teacher raises the student's misaligned-response rate. Same-model rates are Qwen 29.5–45.2%, Gemma 8.2% and Llama under 1%; cross-model transfer is near zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Misalignment can transfer subliminally through semantically innocuous distillation data, mainly between same-model teacher and student pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: For Qwen, bins with a higher teacher preference gap give higher malicious transfer (0.364–0.414 in the top bins versus 0.000 in the lowest). For Llama the rates are flat and low.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How strongly the preference gap predicts transfer of the misaligned trait depends on the model.

fits_no_version.finding: Five tokens carry about 71% (malicious) and 67% (Owl) of the absolute preference-gap mass in Qwen number sequences.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The subliminal trait signal is concentrated in a few token positions, though not necessarily the opening ones.

record.problems: The outcomes relevant to harmful behavior are deliberately induced by teacher conditioning and are not evidence about ordinary safety fine-tuning. Several reported diagnostic conditions use a single seed; uncertainty is not stated for the six-bin rates or token-concentration ratios. Cross-model behavioral results are described as attenuated and model-dependent.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant findings were omitted. Animal-preference outcomes and corridor-control results are outside the claim's harmful-request safety versions; cited results from prior work were not recorded as study results.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning of safety-trained models on harmful examples measuring compliance with harmful requests.
No ordinary or selected benign fine-tuning measuring harmful-request compliance. The number-sequence data carry a deliberately induced misaligned trait, and the measure is open-ended misalignment.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts, and no analysis by response position.
No prefill, suffix or decoding bypasses tested.
No localization of safety in weights or ranks.
No account of why safety alignment is shallow.
No training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens. Corridor regularization constrains drift along a trait-probe direction during distillation.

record.verdict_notes: Agrees with the reader's T6 / cites_only call. The malicious trait comes from an 'evil and misaligned AI' system prompt given to the teacher, so this is deliberate induction. The behaviour measure is misalignment on open-ended questions, not compliance with harmful requests.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning of safety-trained models on a few to a few hundred harmful examples; the malicious trait is deliberately introduced through teacher-conditioned number-sequence distillation.
No ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction fine-tuning measuring harmful-request compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement on harmful prompts, nor a test of whether it is concentrated in early response positions.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes tested as bypasses.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The paper proposes a mechanism for subliminal trait transfer, not an explanation of safety shallowness.
Corridor regularization controls specified trait drift during distillation; it does not train safety beyond the first tokens or test whether such deepening holds up.

relation.reason: Related Work cites safety degradation from fine-tuning, including Qi et al., but the study neither tests nor uses shallow safety alignment as its method.

tranche.reason: The study intentionally induces teacher traits and distills them into students. Under the supplied exclusion for deliberately induced behavior, this does not test a claim version. Its drift mechanism and control concern subliminal trait transfer.

source_check.notes: Table 3 uses the target student's top 10,000 ranked sequences from each 40,000-sequence source pool; its diagonal references are trained controls. Misalignment is judged on eight open-ended questions, rather than harmful-request compliance or first-token KL.
